page: Google Cloud Platform h3-standard-88 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance built on the Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The machine delivers 88 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, entirely eliminating hyperthreading resource contention. It is provisioned with 352.0 GB of memory, equating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The hardware architecture incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 KB of L1 data cache, alongside instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. The system does not feature bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight top-tier capabilities in high-throughput, multi-threaded CPU tasks. The instance achieved 142,603.41 on multi-core stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 94,485.68, placing it in the top decile. In specialized parallel workloads, it scored 61,081.0 in Clang compilation and 105,353.0 in ray tracing. Redis SET operations reached 176.37 million operations per second, accompanied by top-tier static web serving throughput of 139.03 GB/sec and an uncached large-block read memory bandwidth of 469.37 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks register strictly within the average bracket, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,730.0 and single-core stress-ng metric of 1,623.39.

The 1:4 CPU-to-memory allocation makes h3-standard-88 an efficient platform for parallel computational jobs that scale across physical execution units without thread overlap. Tradeoffs focus on the absence of bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block devices, and unexceptional single-core performance. Consequently, the instance is suitable for large-scale Clang/C++ software compilation pipelines, High-Performance Computing (HPC) simulations, ray tracing, and heavily multi-threaded network services.
